newsitem.title: USA: Judge orders dealer to remove Ferrari name.
newsitem.headline: Judge orders dealer to remove Ferrari name.

text.p: A judge on Wednesday gave a the last Ferrari dealer in New York City one day to remove all the Italian automaker's trademarks from his showroom, the latest chapter in an angry dispute between the carmaker and the car salesman.
Ousted dealer Steven Kessler, who is suing to keep his franchise, has accused Ferrari of rolling back the odometers on its posh luxury cars.
Kessler is challenging a decision by Ferrari North America to terminate its franchise with him after 15 years.
He claims Ferrari is trying to drive him out of business in favour of another dealer in suburban Long Island.

Carl Chiappa, a lawyer for Ferrari, said Kessler's contract was terminated in part because Manhattan is not an ideal location for selling its cars due to the ennormous costs of operating a dealership.
He also cited Kessler's "dreadful performance as a Ferrari dealer." He also disputed Kessler's charge that odometers on new Ferraris delivered to his dealership were rolled back to show low mileage.
In a court hearing on Wednesday, Manhattan Supreme Court Judge Elliott Wilk told Kessler he had 24 hours to remove the Ferrari trademarks in his Manhattan showroom.
"Put a red line through the word Ferrari. Put something else on it, something pretty," the judge said.
The Ferrari lawyer also said test drivers in Italy run the sports cars, which cost between $120,000 and $210,000, through trials that accumulate between 75 and 125 miles.
A further court hearing was scheduled for next Wednesday.
